{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table built a large fish (nose on the left, body outline, crossing at the tail neck, forked tail) that traces through from the start with all 111 dominoes connected. My main contribution was on the bottom line: when it was running behind, I picked it up from where it ended and carried it through to the crossing, which helped get the lower body to the tail in time. I also checked the area closely afterward to confirm the joins.

Execution: I laid the bottom run in several builds, extending from the end of the line toward the crossing, then inspected the area to make sure the chain was continuous. After that I kept my hands off the finished work so we didn't risk a bump, which fit the team's agreement and the clock.

Collaboration: I coordinated with Maya on where the bottom run would hand off, stayed clear of her hands, and responded quickly when the plan changed and the start moved to the nose. I cleared what I had laid at the old start and tail so it wouldn't interfere. I also offered ideas, such as adding back-half strokes, and accepted Maya's decision when she preferred not to redraw.

Leadership: I proposed splitting the long bottom line so we could work from both ends, and I kept the table informed about where I was and what I was doing. I helped keep the group focused on the final check and on staying hands-off in the last minutes.", "my_share_percent": 25}
